about.title: Mijung IM
about.subtitle: Pianist of Peace & Nature
about.bioShort: Mijung IM is an international concert pianist known for bringing performance into dialogue with the natural world — from concert halls to the DMZ.
about.bioMedium: Mijung IM is an international concert pianist whose work moves between the traditional concert stage and unconventional sites of performance — forests, borderlands, and spaces marked by conflict. Her recitals are shaped as much by the acoustics of a hall as by the quiet of a landscape, and she is recognized for a repertoire that pairs canonical works with new music written in response to place. She has appeared with orchestras and in recital across North America, Europe, and Asia.
about.bioFull:
Mijung IM is an international concert pianist whose work moves between the traditional concert stage and unconventional sites of performance — forests, borderlands, and spaces marked by conflict. Her recitals are shaped as much by the acoustics of a hall as by the quiet of a landscape, and she is recognized for a repertoire that pairs canonical works with new music written in response to place.

Her performances at the DMZ and in other natural settings have become a signature of her artistic identity, framing the piano recital as an act of reconciliation between people, history, and land. She has appeared with orchestras and in recital across North America, Europe, and Asia, and her work has drawn the attention of presenters and press interested in the intersection of music, peacebuilding, and environmental awareness.

Beyond the stage, she is active in education and community initiatives, working with young musicians and civic organizations to extend the reach of her artistic vision. This section will be replaced with the final approved biography copy.
about.visionBody: For Mijung IM, musical excellence is not an end in itself. Virtuosity becomes meaningful when it serves listening, attentiveness, and human connection. Her performances invite audiences into a space of attentive listening. Rather than projecting emotion outward, she draws listeners inward, allowing musical meaning to emerge through nuance, pacing, resonance, and silence.

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Festivals, foundations, and educational initiatives
projects.plzBody: Founded in 2019 with the support of Gangwon Province, the PLZ Festival reimagines Korea's DMZ border region not only as a symbol of division, but as a Peace and Life Zone. Under Mijung IM's artistic direction, performances were created in railway stations, beaches, forests, churches, botanical gardens, and historic locations.
projects.plzImageCaption: Mijung IM performing on the shore of Korea's East Sea
projects.dmzBody: Appointed as General Director of Gyeonggi Province's DMZ OPEN Festival, Mijung IM curated and led its International Music Festival, bringing together distinguished soloists, major orchestras, and laureates of leading international competitions.
projects.foundationBody: Founded by Mijung IM in 2005, the Music for One Foundation develops artistic and educational programs that connect music with dignity, cultural dialogue, and human development. Its initiatives have included music education and international exchange projects in Cambodia, Myanmar, Tanzania, and India.

home.statementHeadline: Her performances unite technical excellence with contemplative depth.
home.statementTagline: Where music meets silence, nature, and human presence.
home.introBody: Some performances are remembered for their virtuosity. Others remain with us because of the place they create within the listener. Pianist Mijung IM brings these two dimensions together. Her playing combines clarity of tone, technical command, contemplative depth, and a deeply personal sense of musical presence. Whether performing in an established concert hall or in a landscape shaped by history, she approaches music as a living encounter—between sound and silence, memory and hope, the individual and the wider human experience. Through a career spanning the United States, Europe, and Asia, she has developed an artistic identity that is both classically grounded and unmistakably her own.
